items.title: A cartesian square of finite type algebras with surjections keeps the fourth corner of finite type

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma extends the finite type statement for a fibre product of two algebras to a cartesian square indexed by a finite set, and the proof is a 16-line induction. It splits the index set, applies the induction hypothesis to obtain finite generation of the fibre product over the smaller index set, and then observes that the original algebra sits in a fibre product square of the two-algebra shape, to which the earlier statement applies. The two steps are genuine: the splitting of the index set has to be chosen so that the induction hypothesis applies, and the identification of the final square as an instance of the two-factor statement is what closes the induction.
